back: The policy, especially of Neville Chamberlain, of making concessions to Germany to avoid war.
The idea that states would act together against an aggressor, the basis of the League of Nations.

front: What was agreed at Munich in September 1938?
back: The Sudetenland was transferred from Czechoslovakia to Germany; the Czechs were not invited.

front: When did German troops occupy Prague?
When did the Second World War in Europe begin?
back: 1 September 1939, when Germany invaded Poland; Britain and France declared war on 3 September.

front: When did Japan invade Manchuria, and when did full war with China begin?
Why did the League fail to stop aggression?
back: It had no army, the US was absent, and Britain and France would not use force; sanctions on Italy excluded oil.

front: Why did Stalin sign the Nazi-Soviet Pact?
back: He distrusted the West after Munich, wanted time to prepare and gained land in eastern Poland and the Baltic states.

front: Why did Britain and France appease Hitler?
back: Fear of another war, weak armies, economic difficulties, belief that Versailles was unfair and fear of communism.
